correctness.rationale: The Hardy monomial basis yields T e_n=e_(a*n/b) exactly when b divides n, where a=m/gcd(m,k), b=k/gcd(m,k) are coprime; n=0 is the constant invariant direction. For each positive n, maximal powers of a and b give a unique n=a^j b^h c, with a and b not dividing c. If a,b>1, fixed c and j+h=L-1 form one length-L truncated-shift chain; infinitely many c congruent to 1 mod ab give countably infinite multiplicity for every L. If b=1 or a=1 the corresponding families are countably many forward or backward shifts; a=b=1 is I. All powers are partial isometries. Von Neumann inequality bounds p(T) by its maximum on the closed disk; phase vectors in arbitrarily long blocks or shift copies give the reverse norm and Calkin-norm inequality. Weakly null singular sequences and infinite-dimensional kernels/cokernels establish every |lambda|<=1 as Fredholm essential spectral point for m!=k; Neumann series excludes |lambda|>1. The basis action also proves point spectra and strong but not uniform power convergence when b>1. Independent exact divisibility/transition checks on 2,495 indices for five (m,k) pairs passed; the proof, not finite tests, handles all m,k>=2.
residual_risks: Infinite-dimensional spectral conclusion uses standard von Neumann and Fredholm/singular sequence results correctly as known inputs; no formal proof assistant or expert attestation was performed.
